headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress plus customer data creates leakage/compliance risk; pairwise interaction with Taipy is otherwise weakly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest external messages and integrations, so malicious content could reach Taipy only if an operator manually bridges outputs or exports data into Taipy. Taipy shows no input channel or network egress, so the pairwise injection path is not default and is limited by the lack of a documented bridge.
conditions: IF an operator copies Chatwoot message content into Taipy inputs, prompt-like content can influence Taipy workflows.
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two, injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between Chatwoot and Taipy outputs.
Use a one-way export format that strips instructions and markup.
Add a review step before Taipy consumes Chatwoot-derived text.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tagging on transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot explicitly touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Taipy has no declared data classes or egress. The pairwise leakage path is therefore mainly through operator-mediated transfer or shared workspace, not a documented default channel; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records into a shared workspace that Taipy reads, sensitive data can flow into Taipy workflows.
IF Taipy is configured to load files from the same directory as Chatwoot exports, leakage becomes reachable.
mitigations: Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive exports.
Redact customer identifiers before transfer.
Use separate service accounts and storage locations.
Audit Taipy inputs for customer data fields before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and Taipy has none, so there is no direct write-write conflict on shared mutable resources in the profiles. Because neither profile shows filesystem write, git, or overlapping OAuth scopes, the conflict pathway is not evidenced and remains low.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, write conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, concurrent updates can collide.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot and Taipy on separate storage paths.
Avoid shared writable databases.
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports that Taipy could ingest for analytics or automation, but Taipy’s profile does not show verification controls. The pathway is plausible if Taipy treats Chatwoot output as authoritative; uncertainty about the bridge and downstream actions pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes Chatwoot exports without validation, Chatwoot errors can cascade into downstream dashboards or jobs.
IF Taipy is used to trigger automated actions from Chatwoot-derived data, incorrect records can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Taipy ingests Chatwoot data.
Require human approval for any action derived from Chatwoot outputs.
Compare sampled records against source systems daily.
Log and alert on schema mismatches.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and messages, which can include regulated personal data, while Taipy has no declared residency, retention, or certification controls. The pairwise compliance risk is a mismatch if Chatwoot data is moved into Taipy-managed workflows or logs; Taipy is the only relevant compliance surface here, so it is cited alongside Chatwoot.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer data is exported into Taipy logs or persisted datasets, retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF Taipy is deployed in a region or account without the same privacy controls as Chatwoot, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Minimize personal data in any Taipy dataset.
Set explicit retention limits for Taipy artifacts.
Document the lawful basis for each transferred field.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows across both systems.
